name: recipient-field
title: Recipient field
description: The To line of a message: type a name or an address, pick a contact, paste a whole list, and keep addresses that fail visible and marked so they can be fixed.
docs: value and onValueChange speak a list of { email, name } (the name is optional) and the second argument says whether every address passed the check and which did not. Chips whose address fails stay in the list: nothing is dropped, they are drawn with a warning icon and a dashed edge, the reason is written under the field (Not a valid address, or the reason your validate returns; with several, the first one's), and a click or Enter on the chip puts its text back into the field to be fixed. Typing shows contacts (initials, name, address, the match in bold, people already on the line left out) in a listbox the input drives with aria-activedescendant; Enter takes the highlighted contact or, with none, keeps the typed text, and so do a comma, a semicolon and leaving the field. A typed address that matches a contact gets the contact's name. Pasting a list split by commas, semicolons, tabs or line breaks, also "Name <address>" and quoted names with commas, makes one chip per entry. Chips are reached with Left from the start of the text or Backspace in an empty field, then Left and Right, removed with Backspace or Delete (the focus goes to the next chip), edited with Enter or F2; only the input is a tab stop. A chip shows its address, or the reason it failed, as a tooltip. A duplicate and the limit set by max are said in a polite line and to a screen reader, and a paste that did not fit says how many went in. validate replaces the default check and may return a reason. contacts is the pool for suggestions, label and hideLabel name the line, name adds a hidden input with the addresses that passed, and labels renames every phrase.
